To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the facial surface can be represented by the surface metric tensor, and that this tensor can be computed using the surface gradient tensor, and that the surface gradient tensor is a bending invariant of the surface.

(i) the bending-invariant forms of a 3D face surface are invariant under facial expressions and (ii) the bending-invariants can be used to construct expression-invariance representations of 3D faces that can be used for face recognition.
The 3D face shape can be represented by a set of isometry-invariant features that can be computed from the 3D facial surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a 3D face-recognition algorithm, based on isometries of facial surface, that is robust to facial expression and can distinguish between identical twin brothers.
the development of a novel, efficient, accurate and robust 3D face representation, as well as a 3D face identification algorithm.
the development of an expression-invariant 2D face recognition algorithm, based on the analysis of 3D data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D approach is more accurate, more reliable, more robust and more efficient than 2D methods.
our algorithm performs very well in the presence of expressions.
our algorithm is robust to facial expressions and it is more accurate than classical 3D face recognizers, such as the Iterated Closest Point (ICP) and the Point Distribution Models (PDMs).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3D face images are more robust to facial expressions than 2D ones and the 3D information can be efficiently used for face recognition.
we are able to construct a representation of a face, which is invariant to isometric deformations of the face surface, and that we can use this representation for 3D face identification.
the 3D facial surface can be represented by a small set of parameters, which can be computed from a set of 3D facial scans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the facial surface can be represented in a canonical form, which is invariant to facial expressions and can be computed from a small set of points sampled on the surface.
the 3D surface reconstruction stage can be avoided in 3D face analysis.
the facial surface is a highly redundant structure.
